guitar.evidence: Jimi Hendrix's white Fender Stratocaster (played upside-down/restrung for a right-handed guitar as a left-handed player) is one of the most iconic guitar associations in rock history.

tone.target: nasal fuzzed Hendrix strat tone with wah accents and amp grit
tone.profile: nasal fuzzed Hendrix strat tone with wah accents and amp grit
tone.summary: A raw, fuzzed signal chain utilizing a Fuzz distortion, Wah pedal for accents, followed by a British amp model (UK 45) to capture the signature '60s mono bite and controlled feedback.

blocks.purpose: Clean up stray noise inherent in high-gain/fuzz tones.
Provides the core Fuzz Face-style fuzz and raw grit required for Hendrix's tone.
Adds the signature wah accents and vocal filtering characteristic of the era.
Adds subtle mid-range bite and harmonic richness to complement the fuzz without muddying it.
blocks.gap: The Green OD is a general boost; using it here helps shape the single-coil brightness needed after heavy fuzz.

alternatives.reason: A simple clean boost could also work, but Green OD offers more tonal shaping.

blocks.purpose: Simulates the classic Marshall/British tone and controlled feedback associated with '60s rock.
Provides the necessary '60s Marshall-style cabinet voicing and punch.
Shaping the tone to emphasize the bright single-coil bite and cut unnecessary low-end mud from the fuzz.
Optional subtle modulation to add depth without distracting from the raw fuzz tone. (Kept off by default for maximum grit).
blocks.gap: The Chorus is generally too clean, but a very low setting can add dimension.

blocks.purpose: Disabled as per the 'corrections' list (remove delay).
Adds a minimal sense of space and controlled feedback without sounding modern or wet.
blocks.gap: A very subtle Room reverb is used to prevent the fuzz from sounding too dry, maintaining the raw '60s feel.

improvements.summary: Upgrade IR for better '60s Marshall cab realism and punch.

proposals.reason: Enhance the '60s Marshall grit and single-coil bite.
